author: nero_eth
content: What I was doing was bursting the network with batches of late payloads to cause the ELs to do additional validation work it isn't really ready to.

author: nero_eth
content: Basically, the problem I see is that when publishing a late payload, EL clients will receive it from their CL and validate it. If this means the payload of the current block gets delayed (which is the case afaict), then you eat into execution time of the next slot.

author: nero_eth
content: I did 3 such bursts and as you can see, I kept my reth node quite busy during a slot in which it should execute another block:

author: nero_eth
content: This might be fine as the attack costs buying bids (bids don't need to be consecutive slots which helps as otherwise mev would go up). So with 0.1 eth you could "buy" a burst of 10 payloads. My reth node was busy for 6s executing that.

author: nero_eth
content: Not sure there is a clean solution to this, any one could probably something similar today, just with the full block, but because of using the full slot for execution (or min. 6s to be precise), this might be a bigger problem than today(?)

author: nero_eth
content:
Thinking about it more, the solution might just be demoting builders when not releasing a payload. 

Every non released payload could cause work in another slot as long as the slot in which the payload was withhold isn't finalized. So maybe clients should block builders until the slot finalizes (or for 3 epochs to keep things simpler). Then builders cannot collect many withhold payloads that could be released to dos another validator.
